Messages.Author: badger
Messages.Body:
Is the rules team's purpose to change rules/cards to promote a certain
playing segment's views on "balance" and "brokeness" or is it to report
misprinted cards and to clarify card text?

I always thought it was the latter. But to my horror, following 7/7, I
found out I was mistaken. I used to post infrequently on this group -
reserving my messages for questions on how certain cards are played.
But following 7/7, I couldn't stay an outsider any longer. I felt so
strongly that some of the changes have so fundamentally altered the
game, that I nearly threw my computer across the room.

Sure, that's exaggerating a bit, but I was pissed. How audacious could
the RT be? Do they have such power that they could change things with
such a heavy hand?

If anything, the RT has the responsibility to maintain consistency
within the game. The 7/7 rulings have done nothing more than fragment
an already divided play group (ie CL vs NCL). The RT should stay out of
gaming fundamentals and stick with issues that they can back as
absolutely necessary (errata of misprinted cards, etc).

Endless reprints and editions of rules is detrimental to redeveloping a
solid core of players. Such changes are reminiscent of D&D over the
past several years - and look what's happened to that game. I'm
starting to wonder if WOTC purchased TSR's stupidity as well as the
rights to their gaming system.

Badger

I suspect you have misunderstood.

If Chris is referring to the same fix I'm familiar with (in fact I think I
invented it), then it goes more or less as follows (with changes to the
original text in Caps):

"Put this card on a vampire in your uncontrolled region. For each blood
counter you transfer to an uncontrolled vampire during your influence
phase, PUT ONE TOMB COUNTER ON this vampire. EACH TOMB COUNTER ON THIS
VAMPIRE REDUCES HIS CAPACITY BY ONE. Burn this card AND ALL TOMB COUNTERS
when this vampire comes into play."

A similar fix that does more or less the same thing would be to say that
the "Tomb Counters" count as influence, but are not otherwise treated as
blood (thus dropping the reference to capacity reduction, which would
tend to confuse people as to the intent of the fix).

The latter would probably be more readily understood, but is less precise.

>So using the above, you put a ToRIII (which costs 3 pool) on a vampire

>If I understand correctly, then that is a 2 pool loss. Why would anyone
>use ToRIII in this case?

You misunderstand. The suggested fixes of this nature run like this:

Tomb, instead of adding blood, adds SOMETHING counters. Being as these
are not blood counters, they cannot be transferred back so Tomb of
Rameses III (note the correct spelling everyone ;) loses its pool
machine aspect, to some extent.

Now, some people say that the SOMETHING counters should add to a
vampire's blood when it comes out. So, say I put ToRIII on Arika. I
transfer four blood to her this turn and four SOMETHING counters. Next
turn, I put two blood on her and two something counters. She has 12
counters on her now so she comes out. The SOMETHING counters become
blood and she has 12 blood. The extra one drains off. Arika out, 11
blood, tomb burned.

Alternatively, I could have pulled the extra blood back off her in
transfer phase.

Chris' fix works like this. The something counters reduce the capacity
of the vampire in the inactive region by 1 each. So, it brings out the
vampire just as quickly as with the outline given above. Now, depending
on your school of thought, the following can each happen:

1) The vampire comes out. Burn all the -1 counters and give them full
blood

2) The vampire comes out. Burn all the -1 counters and leave them with
however much blood they have (net result, Arika with 6 blood, not 11)

3) The vampire comes out. LEAVE all the -1 counters on the vampire and
leave them with the amount of blood they have (net result, Arika with
only a 5 capacity).

The problems with these fixes are as follows:

A) Book-keeping - many people only have 1 type of counter, so how do you
know which are blood and which are SOMETHING counters. Or do you
remember? etc.

B) When does the pool to a vampire get matched by a SOMETHING counter to
the tomb? To all vampires (in which case, you can get 2 inner circle
out for 14 pool - Tomb and 11 to the OTHER inner circle (ie one without
tomb)) or just this one?

C) Can you transfer back from the vampire with the Tomb on it? If you
can, you could still get out a vampire very cheaply - I'd just put blood
onto a vampire and transfer it back so that all that was bringing it out
were something counters. If a something counter didn't carry over as
blood, then maybe it wouldn't be so bad.

D) If you reduce the capacity of a vampire permanently, do you not
reduce the utility of the big vampires?

Bearing all this in mind, my preferred fix would change this

Card Title: Tomb of Rameses III
Pool: 3
Clan: n/a
Card Type: Master
Card Text: Master: unique location

Put this card on a vampire in your uncontrolled
region. For each blood counter you transfer to an
uncontrolled vampire during your influence phase,

move one counter from the blood bank to this vampire.
Burn this card when this vampire comes into play.

to this:

Card Text: Put this card on a vampire in your uncontrolled region.
For each blood transferred to this vampire in your
influence phase, add a Tomb counter to that vampire. If
you transfer a blood away from this vampire, remove a
Tomb counter. Tomb counters count as blood for the
purpose of moving the vampire to the controlled region.
Burn this card and all Tomb counters when this vampire
comes into play.

I actually think that the elegance of the "capacity" card fix was
compromised by the attempt to make the capacity-reducing counters
permanent. Fix is designed to completely eliminate any blood-generating
potential of this card. It does that handily. To have it have the
further effect of making big vampires small seems contrary to the cards
whole intent, which was to bring out big vampires. LSJ's "Eco-Terrorist"
style fix is then alot truer to the original intent of the card. A card
that introduces 4-capacity IC members to the game seems silly to me. Some
of you are now recognizing this as a problem and suggesting *more* card
text to fix it.

The permanent capacity-counters also create a potentially confusing
situation of large numbers of non-blood counters on ready vampires. This
creates the problem of physically distinguishing different types of
counters. This is less of a problem in the inactive region, where it is
much easier to remember which is which.

Permanent capacity reduction seems favored by those who see big vampires
as a enormous problem. However, I don't think it can be argued that big
vampires have ever been a problem in and of themselves. If old RTI made
big vampires broken, then that is an RTI problem, not a big vampire
problem.

If you feel that a complete elimiation of the card's blood-generating
ability doesn't do enough to fix the card, then I would suggest one other
alteration: The counters go on the tomb, not the vampire. Thus, if it is
destroyed, all benefits are lost, and if stolen, are transfered to a new
Methuselah. It also makes it seem more fitting when the counters are
burned with the Tomb.

Proposed card text (changes in CAPS):

Tomb of Rameses III; Master: Unique Location; 3 pool.

Put this card on a vampire in your uncontrolled region. For each blood
counter you transfer to an uncontrolled vampire during your influence

phase, PUT ONE TOMB COUNTER ON THIS CARD. EACH TOMB COUNTER WILL REDUCE
THE CAPACITY OF THE CHOSEN VAMPIRE BY ONE. Burn this card when this
vampire comes into play.

[The last sentence is identical to the original, but because the counters
go on the Tomb, they are burnt when it comes into play].

One disadvantage of using it for for maximum benefit (ie...accumulating 11
counters to bring out an IC member by paying only the Tomb's 3 pool cost)
is that you must leave the Tomb in play longer -- about 3 turns. This
increases the chance that the Tomb will be contested, stolen, or burned.

This tactic typically works only in the very beginning of the game, when
you still have at least 2 minions on your uncontrolled region and can
afford to spend 14 pool. The 14 pool cost of this tactic is overwhelming,
and only makes sense when you were planning to spend most of it anyway.

When it's later in the game, and you can only afford, say, to spend the
initial 3 pool cost of the Tomb itself, then it will take you alot longer
to bring out a vampire, as you will have to spend time juggling reverse
transfers. The 3 pool loss in such circumstances can be an enormous risk,
when the "blood generator" option is removed.

> Minion Tap doesn't speed you up and doesn't make big vampires cheaper to
> buy - it only makes them cheaper after the fact.

But an empty IC member *should* be cheaper than an IC member filled to
capacity, and by a significant amount. Getting an empty IC member in 3
turns for 3 extra pool in a "2 for the price of one" deal that actually
costs you a total pool outlay of 14 does not seem unreasonable to me.

> (They could be
> Rushed and lose lots of blood before they can be Minion Tapped, for
> example.) And even so, Minion Tap is (in my opinion) one of the
> best master cards in the game.

And the Tomb can be stolen, burned, or contested. The longer you leave it
in play, the more likely this is to happen.

vamp is still in play and can still come back out.

frequently and sometimes drastically - not only as a result of getting
beaten up, but due to use of Blood Dolls, actions or modifiers or
reactions that cost blood, Minion Taps, Fifth Traditions, whatever.

: > out that Tomb provides.

: Some of this speed will be lost if he has to hunt on his first turn, fifth

Of course, by spending 1 more pool, you can have 1 blood on the second
IC when it comes out, so that it will never have to hunt. In this
case, the IC can receive 5th tradition (but can't do it to himself,
short of house rules) on his first minion phase, perform
whatever action he wants, and get Minion Tapped on his second master
phase. (One turn later than he can be Minion tapped if he comes out
full. If you're worried about not using that master phase, why not
Minion Tap the IC that *did* come out full?)

: > : in play, the more likely this is to happen.

the tomb provides a much greater incentive for this sort of tactic, and
will tend to cause it to occur with greater frequency. This sort of loss
becomes more damaging, as, unlike the old tomb, a lost fixed tomb will not
repay its worth *at all*.

frequently, but nonetheless they are readily available counters to a fixed
tomb, that make playing the Tomb a significant risk, especially if done
for maximum benefit. The ebb and flow of the metagame will make sure they
come into play more frequently if you give them a good reason. Lets not
forget that you are unlikely to afford the 14 pool needed beyond the
beginning of your game, so if you are playing for maximum benefit (the 2
IC members that we seem to have settled on as the focus of this debate),
then you are likely to have few, if any, minions in play to stop an Arson,

weenies generally. Big vampire decks can be abusive, strictly because of
the overpowered nature of a handful of cards, notably RTI and Mind Rape.

Both these actions are costly in terms of blood, and a no-blood-gain tomb
does not give you any extra blood to power these actions.

If those actions are overpowered, it is those cards that need fixing. The
Tomb itself is overpowered because of the blood-gain effect, not because,
as intended, it really does help bring out big vampires.

> All they get now from Tomb (with the -1 cap counters, non-
> permanent) is big vampires on the cheap. This is a Very Good Thing
> for a pool gain deck. And no, they're not unbeatable, but then,
> no deck is.

Empty vampires are not that useful for a Minion Tap. This is why
Information Highway is so much more effective for such decks than a
no-blood-gain Tomb.

> : Besides, the problem with the old Tomb was that it was effective in
> : pracically *any* deck, not just in specialized Big Minion Blood Generator
> : Decks. For a card to be expecially useful in specialized decks is not
> : unreasonable.
>
> True, but it shouldn't be crazy useful.

And it is not, if you remove the blood-gain effect.

> : > The 14 pool cost is big, yes, but it gets you two IC members. Those
> : > would cost you 22 pool if you had to buy them the hard way.
>
> : Doing it "The hard way" only costs you only 11 pool before you get an
> : opportunity to replenish your supply with a Minion Tap (for up to 11
> : pool). Doing it with the no-blood-gain Tomb costs 14 before you get this
> : chance, 3 of which goes to the blood bank and is unavailable to be
> : Minion Tapped back. "The hard way" gives me 22 pool for minion taps,
> : whereas the no-blood-gain Tomb only gives me 11.
>
> It only gives you 11 up front. Because you have the big vampires in
> play, the opportunity is there to do more Minion Tap tricks later.

The more "Minion Tap" tricks later are not the result of the Tomb. They
are the result of other cards, like Giant's Blood or 5th Tradition. If
you think those cards are overpowered, perhaps we should be discussing
that instead. A no-blood-gain Tomb does not grant you a Minion-Tap Ready
minion, and that is a serious disadvantage in a Minion Tap/Blood Gain
deck.

I might also point out that, since one cannot typically do more than 1
Minion Tap per turn, having a large number of vampires available to be
Minion Tapped does not offer the same benefit.

> Even without putting free blood on the vampire, Tomb still gets out
> big vampires at reduced cost.

Yes, I agree that it does do that. Reduced cost *and* reduced value.

> : > Blood on vampires is transient at best, and frequently ephemeral. It
> : > is not nearly as important as *having* the vampire.
>
> : OK, but if blood on vampires is transient and ephemeral, then empty IC
> : members must also be transient and ephemeral. If one can easily cause a
> : full vampire to burn blood, then how much harder is it to torporize or
> : burn an empty one?
>
> Well, to burn an empty vamp requires either additional aggravated
> damage, Decapitate, or diablerie, usually. Burning vampires was
> originally supposed to be difficult, and recently it's become fairly
> difficult again. Torporizing is easier, of course, but a torporous
> vamp is still in play and can still come back out.

Rescuing Torporized Vampires normally requires that important resource:
Blood. With a no-blood-gain TOR, you have much less of this important
resource.

I realize that empty vampires have value. This is why Minion Tapping (and
Blood Dolls) are profitable. You can recover an amount of pool equal to a
vampire's entire cost, yet still retain part of the vampires value in
play. This does not change the fact that empty vampires are worth much
less than full ones.



This alters the equation, because if you do this you are no longer
bringing out 2 IC members for 14 pool. (Only 3 pool for the extra IC
member, was I believe your argument). Now you appear to be conceding that
this extreme example is not really worthwhile after all, and it is best to
have one IC member come out with one pool. Perhaps its a minor point, but
perhaps you should then stop arguing that 3 extra pool and no extra
transfers is such a great bargain, if in fact 4 extra pool and 1 extra
transfer gets you a better value for your cost.

> In this
> case, the IC can receive 5th tradition (but can't do it to himself,
> short of house rules)

I hope you don't play with such house rules :( IC members definitely
should NOT have access to Prince/Justicar cards, especially 5th tradition.
They are already overpowered without such benefits.

In any event, we have deviated again from your original extreme example of
2 IC members for 14 pool. Clearly 10-capacity Princes and Justicars, not
IC members, are the ideal vampires for a Minion-Tap/5th-Tradition Deck.
So we are now talking of paying 14 pool for 2 minions that might have cost
20 (not 22). You save 6 blood, and return get 9 less blood on your
vampires. In a deck that relies on Minion Taps for blood gain, that is
hardly such a bargain.

> on his first minion phase, perform
> whatever action he wants, and get Minion Tapped on his second master
> phase. (One turn later than he can be Minion tapped if he comes out
> full. If you're worried about not using that master phase, why not
> Minion Tap the IC that *did* come out full?)

Well, again, we obviously should be talking Princes, not IC members. They
cannot *both* be IC members now, can they?

5th tradition is a powerful card, but whoever is playing it better have
serious stealth, else you will be blocked and your plans ruined. TOR, 5th
tradition, stealth, Minion tap is alot more involved and risky than the
more beneficial combo of Info Highway/Minion Tap, and also leaves your
investement more vulnerable to rush and diablerie.

> : > : And the Tomb can be stolen, burned, or contested. The longer you leave it
> : > : in play, the more likely this is to happen.
> : >
> : > Yeah, same for Information Highway, but does that make it less useful
> : > when you get it early?
>
> : I am convinced, that, on balance, Info Highway is comparable to, and
> : perhaps better than a no-blood-gain Tomb. Would you like a point by point
> : comparison?
>
> Sure. It seems to me that the 3 pool cost of Tomb is clearly worthwhile
> given that it produces two extra transfers a turn and doesn't require
> you to spend pool equal to capacity of the vamps you bring out.
>
> : In any event, the past benefits of Info Highway are not lost when it is
> : burned. Nor were the past benefits of Old Tomb. Many versions of
> : No-Blood-Gain Tomb allow all benefits to be lost or stolen with it, such
> : that if you lose it before you get your vampire, you have nothing to show
> : for it but 3 less pool. If such were the case you would take a risk by
> : leaving it in play longer, which is not a factor with the likes of Info
> : Highway.
>
> This is the only drawback that Tomb has compared to Info Highway.

You ought to be able to think of a few other ways without me pointing it
out to you. Come on, you're intelligent! Let's see what you can come up
with.

> And it seems to me that even if the card were only good in the early game,
> that doesn't excuse it being too good when you get it early.

If you look below, you will find that Info Highway does better.

> Risk is all well and good, but this isn't the stock market; excessive
> returns aren't justified by the possibility of losing it all.

Here's my comparison of Info Highway to a No-Blood-Gain Tomb. I am
assuming that in each case the deck is a simple blood-gain deck using 5th
Tradition, Minion Tap and Stealth, with a crypt full of 10 capacity
Princes and Justicars with Obfuscate. In each case, the Tomb or Info
Highway is played on one's first turn. It is assumed that you are the
second person playing, and so would normally get two transfers on your
first turn

Turn #1

A) Play IH. Transfer 4 blood to Queen Anne. Pool=26.
B) Play TOR on Lucian. Transfer 2 blood to Queen Anne. Pool=25.

Turn #2

A) Play Parthenon. Transfer 6 pool to Queen Anne. She comes out with
10. Pool=18.
B) Play Parthenon. Transfer 4 pool to Queen Anne. Pool=19.

Turn #3

A) Minion Tap Queen Anne for 9. She plays 5th Trad. Transfer 6 pool to
Lucian. Pool=21.
B) Transfer 1 blood to Lucian, 2 to Queen Anne, and 1 to Francois Villon.
Queen Anne and Lucian come out simultaneously, Lucian with 1 blood, and
Queen Anne with 10. Pool=15.

Turn #4

A) Play Elesium; Minion Tap Queen Anne for 9. She plays 5th
Tradition. Transfer 4 more pool to Lucian, and 2 to Francois Villon.
Lucian enters play. Pool=24.
B) Play another TOR on Harrod. Minion Tap Queen Anne for 9. Queen Anne
plays 5th Tradition. Lucian plays 5th Tradition. Transfer 4 blood to
Francois Villon. Pool=17.

Turn #5

A) Minion Tap Queen Anne and Lucian for 9 each. Both play 5th Tradition.
Transfer 6 blood to Francois Villon. Pool=36.
B) Minion Tap Queen Anne and Lucian for 9 each. Both play 5th Tradition.
transfer 4 more blood to Francois Villon. Pool=31.

Well that's about as far as I want to go for now. I think the TOR may be
catching up, but it's taking a while, and it has so far required that 2 of
them be played. Performance is in some ways comparable, but the TOR deck
fell as low as 12 pool before starting to climb (putting it dangerously
close to an oust) whereas the Highway deck never went under 18.

Lupus Australis (jbwh...@dorsai.org) wrote:

: On 21 Aug 1998, Joshua Duffin wrote:

: > Lupus Australis (jbwh...@dorsai.org) wrote:
: >
: > : Actually, your opponents have 2 turns instead of 1 in which to destroy

: > : it, steal it, or contest it. The opportunity is doubled.
: >
: > Yes, it is. From almost zero, to slightly more than zero. ;-) It's
: > still not a big disadvantage.

: I suspect you are thinking of "Old Tomb" precedent when you make this
: statement. A fixed tomb that allows benefits to be lost or stolen with
: the tomb provides a much greater incentive for this sort of tactic, and
: will tend to cause it to occur with greater frequency. This sort of loss
: becomes more damaging, as, unlike the old tomb, a lost fixed tomb will not
: repay its worth *at all*.

True, it's worse when your Tomb gets blown up. But if you're
using new Tomb the fast way, two turns of opportunity is still not
a whole lot of time.

: Cards like Arson, Kine Dominance, and Disputed Territory may not be played

: frequently, but nonetheless they are readily available counters to a fixed
: tomb, that make playing the Tomb a significant risk, especially if done
: for maximum benefit. The ebb and flow of the metagame will make sure they
: come into play more frequently if you give them a good reason. Lets not
: forget that you are unlikely to afford the 14 pool needed beyond the
: beginning of your game, so if you are playing for maximum benefit (the 2
: IC members that we seem to have settled on as the focus of this debate),
: then you are likely to have few, if any, minions in play to stop an Arson,
: or vote against a Disputed Territory against your initial tomb.

These are card vs card answers. The only thing that makes these better
than 'play Deflection/Telepathic Misdirection vs RtI' is that Arson
is disciplineless.

Sure, they're good if they happen to fit into your deck well, but
they aren't a justification. Sure, they can punish Tomb players by
using the metagame, but that doesn't balance the Tomb.

: You continue to talk about buying vamps as though an empty vampire is

: equal in value to a full one. Perhaps I should ask you how much *you*
: think is the relative difference in value between a full and an empty IC
: member? A full one is clearly worth 11 pool in 2.75 turns. How much
: would you say an empty one is worth?

I can't say for sure. Maybe 5-7 pool? I do think it's more than 3-4
pool. Do you have an exact figure you think they're worth?

(I'm not so sure a full IC is 'worth' 11 pool in 2.75 turns, either.
That's what it normally costs, but what a vampire is 'worth' is
a pretty complicated question I think.)

: > These decks are *less* effective without the bloodgain part of Tomb,

: > but not *that* much less.

: Yes, *that* much less, specifically, up to 11 blood per Tomb waiting to be
: minion tapped. What the heck are you talking about "not that much
: less"???? This is *especially* significant in a Minion Tap/Blood-Gain
: deck. Probably about 9 to 11 pool worth of significance!!!

Not having the blood on the vampire means you may not get the pool
as quickly; it doesn't mean you don't get it at all.

: > What makes [big vampire Tomb-using decks] *far* less effective than

: > they used to be is that they can no longer abuse RtI, Mind Rape, and
: > Soul Gem like they used to (in the archetypal Meet the Inner Circle
: > decks).

: The Tomb was designed to lend a hand to big vampires. I see nothing wrong
: with this, since big vampires are rather underpowered compared to multiple
: weenies generally. Big vampire decks can be abusive, strictly because of
: the overpowered nature of a handful of cards, notably RTI and Mind Rape.

As I think I mentioned elsewhere, I've never heard of the Tomb
resulting in the use of the big vampires that are really underpowered.
Nobody gets out Apollonius with a Tomb. What the Tomb did was make
the *good* big vampires a bargain at half the price.

: Both these actions are costly in terms of blood, and a no-blood-gain tomb

: does not give you any extra blood to power these actions.

: If those actions are overpowered, it is those cards that need fixing. The
: Tomb itself is overpowered because of the blood-gain effect, not because,
: as intended, it really does help bring out big vampires.

Sure, any overpowered card needs fixing. These particular ones worked
especially well with the big vampires that Tomb made cheaper.

My argument is not that "Tomb with impermanent cap-reducing counters
that works with transfers to other vampires" is grossly overpowered.
I would just prefer that either the counters be permanent or that
Tomb only produce counters when you transfer to the en-Tombed vampire.

: Empty vampires are not that useful for a Minion Tap. This is why

: Information Highway is so much more effective for such decks than a
: no-blood-gain Tomb.

Yeah, sure it is. ;-)

: > It only gives you 11 up front. Because you have the big vampires in

: > play, the opportunity is there to do more Minion Tap tricks later.

: The more "Minion Tap" tricks later are not the result of the Tomb. They
: are the result of other cards, like Giant's Blood or 5th Tradition. If
: you think those cards are overpowered, perhaps we should be discussing
: that instead. A no-blood-gain Tomb does not grant you a Minion-Tap Ready
: minion, and that is a serious disadvantage in a Minion Tap/Blood Gain
: deck.

: I might also point out that, since one cannot typically do more than 1
: Minion Tap per turn, having a large number of vampires available to be
: Minion Tapped does not offer the same benefit.

Well, with only one big vamp, you can still do one minion tap a turn,
yes. But even Minion Tap/5th Tradition decks have to do something to
kill their prey, right? Having more than one big vampire allows
you to take more useful actions, etc, etc. If one of your vampires
gets beaten up or something and winds up out of blood, then another
can 5th Trad it, instead of just being screwed.

: Rescuing Torporized Vampires normally requires that important resource:

: Blood. With a no-blood-gain TOR, you have much less of this important
: resource.

: I realize that empty vampires have value. This is why Minion Tapping (and
: Blood Dolls) are profitable. You can recover an amount of pool equal to a
: vampire's entire cost, yet still retain part of the vampires value in
: play. This does not change the fact that empty vampires are worth much
: less than full ones.

See, I'm not so sure about the 'much' in 'much less'. I've played
a lot of combat decks, and in my experience, it often doesn't matter
whether Anvil has 1 blood on him or 6. He can still Bum Rush, Torn
Signpost, Immortal Grapple, Blur, Taste of Vitae and end up full.
I've played some pool-gain decks, and Emerson Bridges can play
Majesty, cast votes, and play Skin of Steel (once) just as well
when he has 1 blood as when he has 8.

Have you ever played against a vote deck using Banishment? Were you
unconcerned about having your low-blood vampires Banished, because
they weren't worth as much?

Blood on vampires is a resource the vampires can use to play cards.
It is very renewable. Vampires in play is a resource the methuselah
can use to further his strategy. They are less renewable. This is
why it's more important *whether* you have a vampire in play to use
than *how much* blood they have on them.

[a bunch of my points snipped - how come you didn't reply to these? ;-) ]

: > Of course, by spending 1 more pool, you can have 1 blood on the second

: > IC when it comes out, so that it will never have to hunt.

: This alters the equation, because if you do this you are no longer
: bringing out 2 IC members for 14 pool. (Only 3 pool for the extra IC
: member, was I believe your argument). Now you appear to be conceding that
: this extreme example is not really worthwhile after all, and it is best to
: have one IC member come out with one pool. Perhaps its a minor point, but
: perhaps you should then stop arguing that 3 extra pool and no extra
: transfers is such a great bargain, if in fact 4 extra pool and 1 extra
: transfer gets you a better value for your cost.

It gets you more speed. Whether that's a better value will depend
on the situation and your tactics.

: > In this

: > case, the IC can receive 5th tradition (but can't do it to himself,
: > short of house rules)

: I hope you don't play with such house rules :( IC members definitely
: should NOT have access to Prince/Justicar cards, especially 5th tradition.
: They are already overpowered without such benefits.

No, I've never played like that. Your example seemed to imply IC
members doing 5th Tradition for each other.

: In any event, we have deviated again from your original extreme example of

: 2 IC members for 14 pool. Clearly 10-capacity Princes and Justicars, not
: IC members, are the ideal vampires for a Minion-Tap/5th-Tradition Deck.
: So we are now talking of paying 14 pool for 2 minions that might have cost
: 20 (not 22). You save 6 blood, and return get 9 less blood on your
: vampires. In a deck that relies on Minion Taps for blood gain, that is
: hardly such a bargain.

It's pretty good. ;-) Getting out plentiful IC members is not as
handy as it once was, since RtI and Mind Rape are no longer so useful.
But they do still have plenty of good points - built in +2 bleed, 4
votes, can be Minion Tapped for 10, lots of disciplines, often have
good special abilities...

: 5th tradition is a powerful card, but whoever is playing it better have

: serious stealth, else you will be blocked and your plans ruined. TOR, 5th
: tradition, stealth, Minion tap is alot more involved and risky than the
: more beneficial combo of Info Highway/Minion Tap, and also leaves your
: investement more vulnerable to rush and diablerie.

But Info Highway/Minion Tap will leave your vampires empty without
5th Tradition involved.

In my metagame experience, intercept is rarely a winning strategy, so
you don't see a lot of it.

: > : In any event, the past benefits of Info Highway are not lost when it is

: > : burned. Nor were the past benefits of Old Tomb. Many versions of
: > : No-Blood-Gain Tomb allow all benefits to be lost or stolen with it, such
: > : that if you lose it before you get your vampire, you have nothing to show
: > : for it but 3 less pool. If such were the case you would take a risk by
: > : leaving it in play longer, which is not a factor with the likes of Info
: > : Highway.
: >
: > This is the only drawback that Tomb has compared to Info Highway.

: You ought to be able to think of a few other ways without me pointing it
: out to you. Come on, you're intelligent! Let's see what you can come up
: with.

Ummm... Tomb doesn't give you any actual extra transfers, only
virtual transfers.

(Tomb also costs 3 more than IH, which is kinda like a drawback.)

: > And it seems to me that even if the card were only good in the early game,

: > that doesn't excuse it being too good when you get it early.

: If you look below, you will find that Info Highway does better.

In one scenario, yeah... ;-)

: > Risk is all well and good, but this isn't the stock market; excessive

: > returns aren't justified by the possibility of losing it all.

: Here's my comparison of Info Highway to a No-Blood-Gain Tomb. I am
: assuming that in each case the deck is a simple blood-gain deck using 5th
: Tradition, Minion Tap and Stealth, with a crypt full of 10 capacity
: Princes and Justicars with Obfuscate. In each case, the Tomb or Info
: Highway is played on one's first turn. It is assumed that you are the
: second person playing, and so would normally get two transfers on your
: first turn

Note that IH's efficacy is greater the earlier in the game you play
(ie it's even more good if you were the first person to play).
Suppose we have both players go fourth, where Tomb's full benefit
becomes available:

Turn 1:

A) Play Tomb on Queen Anne; transfer 4 to Queen Anne; pool=23.

B) Play IH; transfer 6 to Queen Anne; pool=24.

Turn 2:

A) Play Parthenon; transfer 4 to Anson; Anne comes out with 4 blood;
pool=17.

B) Play Parthenon; transfer 4 to Anne, 2 to Anson; Anne comes out
full; pool=16.

Turn 3:

A) Minion Tap Anne for 3, Tomb on Francois; Anne 5thTrads; transfer
4 to Anson; Anson comes out with 8; pool=13.

B) Minion Tap Anne for 9; Anne 5thTrads; transfer 6 to Anson; Anson
comes out with 8; pool=19.

Turn 4:

A) Minion Tap Anne for 9, Anson for 7; both 5thTrad; transfer 2 to
Francois, 2 to Anneke; Francois comes out with 2; pool=25.

B) Minion Tap Anne for 9, Anson for 7; both 5thTrad; transfer 6
to Francois; pool=29.

Turn 5:

A) Minion Tap Anne for 9, Anson for 7, Tomb on Anneke; all three
vamps 5thTrad; transfer 4 to Anneke; Anneke comes out with 6; pool=34.

B) Minion Tap Anne for 9, Anson for 7; both 5thTrad; transfer 4 to
Francois, 2 to Anneke; Francois comes out with 10; pool=39.

[Turn 6:

A) Minion Tap Anne for 9, Anson for 7, Francois for 9; all four
5thTrad; pay 1 for a new vampire to look at; pool=58.

B) Minion Tap Anne for 9, Anson for 7, Francois for 9; all three
5thTrad; transfer 6 to Anneke; pool=58.]

---
In this example, the Tomb user gets out Queen Anne on turn 2 (should
be early enough to forestall any threat of early ousting), Anson
on 3, Francois on 4, Anneke on 5. IH user gets Queen Anne on 2,
Anson on 3, Francois on 5. IH user usually has more pool but fewer
vampires to do other things with (some of the 5th Trad action ends
up being superfluous when you can't Tap all your vampires every
turn).

: Well that's about as far as I want to go for now. I think the TOR may be

: catching up, but it's taking a while, and it has so far required that 2 of
: them be played. Performance is in some ways comparable, but the TOR deck
: fell as low as 12 pool before starting to climb (putting it dangerously
: close to an oust) whereas the Highway deck never went under 18.

(Actually, in your scenario, the ToR deck never went below 15 at an
end of turn, as far as I could tell.)

As long as there are infinite Minion Taps available, why not also
allow infinite Tombs? ;-)

Seriously, these ideal scenarios probably don't tell us all that much
about how the cards (and decks) perform in real life. (Also note
that these decks would do even better if they used both Tomb and
IH.)

My impression is that Tomb is at least as good at getting out big
vampires fast as Info Highway. It is (fixed version) probably
useful in fewer decks. This may actually make it more useful to decks
of the Minion Tap/5th Tradition variety, since Info Highway is more
likely to be contested (since it's useful to weenie decks as well
as big-vamp decks).

Man, these posts have gotten long. See what happens when you argue
with people who don't just post a few lines of unsupported assertions?
(You get hundreds of lines of unsupported assertions instead! ha ha.)

Josh
